step: G test pins (FD-6 class, R-6, R-10): suites that pinned a moved path, a dropped name or the pre-R-10 shell construction read the migrated tree
why: Each hunk is the smallest edit that makes a suite state the same invariant over the migrated tree. None weakens a check. (1) proportion-register and typed-track-seam compare literal path strings that F-1 does not read as paths (a report line, a generated manifest's @import list); the L7.2 carve moved those sheets. (2) dissolve finds its AUTH row in a closed BJ record (BAND-FEEDBACK-MOTION.md §PRM-AUTHORIZED-SET), which is never rewritten and spells the sheet by its old path; the row is found by the sheet's own name, which survives any move, and the next lines still check the row's selector and digest. (3) g-dock-lattice counts the controls/ partials of the band; the L4.4 purity row added specular.css, the door's former :where() group, as a fifth. (4) boot-graph's source arm pinned the leaf construction R-10 cures: the async boundary now imports the ./aurora subpath dynamically, and the eager ground reads the ./aurora-config leaf (P3-R5); the byte arm is unchanged and judges the chunk cost. (5) public-surface names the rows R-6 dropped (DAMPING and SNAP_THRESHOLD ship on ./motion-core alone; useDockCtaReceive on ./motion alone).
